The facts in brief leading to the initiation State vs . Satender & Ors on 16 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66336858/
1 of criminal proceedings against the accused persons may be summed up as under:-
Accused Satender got married to one Monika (since deceased) on 30.11.2012.

During the period between 30.11.2012 to 07.10.2013, at H. No. 675, Mandoli Village, Delhi,
all accused persons in pursuance of their common intention subjected Monika (since deceased) to harassment and cruelty on pretext of demand of dowry and other unlawful demands and thereby all accused committed an offence under Section 498-A IPC r/w 34 IPC.

Further, soon before 07.10.2013, at the aforesaid address all accused persons subjected deceased Monika to cruelty and harassment physically and mentally in connection with their unlawful demand of dowry and thereby leading her to commit suicide (unnatural death), otherwise than under normal circumstances, thereby committed offence of 'dowry death' as defined in Section 304- B (1) IPC and punishable under Section 304-B (2) IPC r/w 34 IPC.

Further, prior to 30.11.2012 i.e. date of marriage, at the aforesaid aforesaid address i.e. matrimonial house of deceased, all accused in pursuance of their common intention, took dowry and after marriage demanded more dowry as consideration for marriage between Monika and accused Satender and thus, all committed an offence punishable under Section 3 and 4 Dowry Prohibition Act State vs. Satender & Ors Police Station: Harsh Vihar r/w 34 IPC.

The tendency of the Court should not be that since a young bride has died after marriage, now somebody must be held culprit and the noose must be made to fit some neck.
25.
It is a cardinal principal of criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution is supposed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt by leading reliable, cogent and convincing evidence.
Similarly, it is established principle that the prosecution is supposed to stand on its own legs and cannot derive benefits whatsoever from the weakness, if any, in the defence of accused.

The burden of proof of the version of prosecution in criminal trial, throughout trial lies on prosecution and never shifts to accused who is entitled to benefit of every reasonable doubt in the prosecution story and any such doubt entitles him to acquittal.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Accused persons are facing trial having been charged for the offence u/s 498-A/304-B IPC and u/s 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act r/w Section 34 IPC.
Accused Satender got married to one Monika (since deceased) on 30.11.2012.
During the period between 30.11.2012 to 07.10.2013, at H. No. 675, Mandoli Village, Delhi,
all accused persons in pursuance of their common intention subjected Monika (since deceased) to harassment and cruelty on pretext of demand of dowry and other unlawful demands and thereby all accused committed an offence under Section 498-A IPC r/w 34 IPC.
Further, soon before 07.10.2013, at the aforesaid address all accused persons subjected deceased Monika to cruelty and harassment physically and mentally in connection with their unlawful demand of dowry and thereby leading her to commit suicide (unnatural death), otherwise than under normal circumstances, thereby committed offence of 'dowry death' as defined in Section 304- B (1) IPC and punishable under Section 304-B (2) IPC r/w 34 IPC.

When the prosecution shows that 'soon before her death such woman has been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand of dowry', a presumption of causation arises against the accused under Section 113B of the Evidence Act.
Thereafter, the accused has to rebut this statutory presumption.

It is significant to observe that none of the witnesses particularly the mother of victim ever talked to any of the accused persons regarding the alleged demand of Rs. 10 lacs and a plot after birth of a girl child to the victim.
The accused persons were never confronted regarding such a demand.
No protest was ever raised by the family of victim to the in-laws of their daughter.

It is a settled proposition of law that any amount or gift given by the family of bride at or after the birth of a child does not strictly constitute 'dowry'.
Supposingly, the amount of Rs. 10 lacs was demanded by accused persons pursuant to the birth of a girl child, it is highly improbable that the same would be considered 'dowry' for the purposes of Section 304B IPC dealing with the offence of dowry death.
In this regard, Hon'be Apex Court in Ran Singh vs. State 2008 (1) RCR (Cr) 894 SC and Phool Singh vs. State 2010 (3) LRC 6 Delhi held that payments which are customary payments e.g. given at the time of birth of a child or other ceremonies as are prevalent in different societies are not covered by the expression 'dowry'.
22.

It is not the case of prosecution at all that victim Monika disclosed any cruelty or harassment at the hands of her in- laws in connection with or for demand of dowry while she talked to her mother.

"In our view, onus was on the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt the ingredient of Section 498A, IPC and the essential ingredient of offence under Section 498A is that the accused, as the husband of deceased, has subjected her to cruelty as defined in th explanation to Section 498A, IPC.
In the opinion of this Court, prosecution must have established existence of 'proximate and live link'
between the dowry death and cruelty or harassment for dowry demand by the husband or his relatives (As reiterated by Hon'be Supreme Court in Satbir Singh V. State of Haryana, 28.05.2021).
In the present case, State vs. Satender & Ors Police Station: Harsh Vihar prosecution could not establish existence of any such link between the alleged dowry death of victim Monika and the alleged cruelty or harassment for dowry.

However, Court can not get swayed by emotions arising out of the death of a young bride and thereby presume the culpability of the accused.
